**suggestion (bug_risk):** The type suggests exactly one of `url` or `b64` is present, but the typing allows both or neither.

Given the invariant, the current `{ url?: string; b64?: string }` shape is too permissive because it admits both fields or neither. Consider encoding this as a union such as `{ id: string; url: string; b64?: never } | { id: string; b64: string; url?: never }` (or a tagged union) so the type system enforces that exactly one representation is used.

✅ Addressed in d8814f63d8b4dbccae3817203921829fa9fd2731: `ProviderImage` is now a discriminated-style union (`{ id; url; b64?: never } | { id; b64; url?: never }`), so the type system enforces that exactly one of `url` or `b64` is present.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Update seam ledger before deleting required artifacts**

Deleting this mock (and the companion `src/lib/adapters/image-generation.adapter.ts`) leaves `docs/seams.md` line 33 pointing at paths that no longer exist. In the inspected workflow, `npm run verify` runs `npm run chamber:lock` first, and `scripts/chamber-lock.mjs` parses `docs/seams.md`, checks each listed mock/adapter path, and exits with `Chamber Lock: missing required seam artifacts.` whenever any listed artifact is missing. This means CI verification for every PR will fail until the legacy ImageGenerationSeam row is removed or changed to `N/A`/the self-contained artifacts.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

The new contract comment claims ProviderImage has exactly one of `url` or `b64` present, but the type/validators allow both or neither, and the live adapter can currently produce both-undefined (or `null` without normalization). Either enforce the invariant in the type/validators, or soften the comment so it doesn't promise something the contract doesn't guarantee.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep provider image validation one-of**

After this contract change, `ProviderImage` is a strict one-of shape, but the runtime schema used by `validateImageGenerationResult` and `GalleryStoreSeam` validation still has both `url` and `b64` as optional fields. In any contract test or mock/adapter validation path that relies on `src/lib/seams/image-generation-seam/validators.ts`, malformed outputs like `{ id: 'x' }` or images containing both representations will still pass despite violating this new seam contract, so the schema should be changed to a union/refinement that enforces exactly one representation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
